arrangement.description: Study 01 variation A arpeggio with harmonic reference A. The chord is not inside the arpeggio file.

note_policy: note-only MIDI. Filters, chorus, and slides are not encoded.
range_statement: Arpeggios are monophonic, MIDI 48 to 84. Harmonic references use MIDI 48 to 76, at most four notes, and are not part of the core count. C4 is 60.
seed_meaning: Seeds identify studies. Nothing is random.
stack_warning: Use either the combined arrangement or the separate parts. Do not stack the part files on top of the combined file.

studies.accent: Velocity climbs inside the bar and peaks on the fifth attack. Phrase 3 adds another step to that peak.
studies.harmonic_rhythm: Source harmony: Am, F, C, G. Each chord lasts 4 bars.
studies.identity: Horizon Ladder moves through Am, F, C, G. Variation A is six eighths climbing from the downbeat, with a gap before each attack and a rest through beat 4. The register shifts with each chord. Variation B is a descent from the high chord tones, entering on the second 16th. It is not the reverse of the same bar of variation A. In the opening phrase, bar 1 of B is the reverse of bar 4 of A.
studies.layering: One arpeggio channel. The chord is the harmonic reference on its own channel and in its own file. Do not merge the two files into one part.
studies.limitations: Pair arpeggio A with harmonic reference A, and B with B. The arpeggio is monophonic and leaves gaps, so notes inside that file do not overlap. The harmonic reference keeps its own voicing and timing. The arrangement is only study 01.

studies.rhythm_b: a descent from the high chord tones, entering on the second 16th. It is not the reverse of the same bar of variation A. In the opening phrase, bar 1 of B is the reverse of bar 4 of A
studies.source_harmony: The harmonic reference holds Am, F, C, G as written triads. It is a separate file and it is not part of the core count. Variation A stacks a close triad from the downbeat, louder on the top note. F and G sit an octave higher than Am and C.
